paper_metadata.title: Room temperature tensile properties and texture prior to and following high temperature deformation in a superplastic AZ31 magnesium alloy

evidence.quote: Room temperature tensile properties and texture prior to and following high temperature deformation were examined in a superplastic AZ31 magnesium alloy with relatively coarse grains.

samples.material_state: superplastically deformed (50% elongation at 673 K, low strain rate)

evidence.quote: The specimens were deformed to nominal strains of 50 and 75% at high temperatures of 673 and 723 K and at various strain rates.

samples.material_state: superplastically deformed (75% elongation at 673 K, low strain rate)

evidence.quote: The specimens were deformed to nominal strains of 50 and 75% at high temperatures of 673 and 723 K and at various strain rates.
The jump strain rate tensile test was carried out in air at a temperature of 673 K and a base strain rate of 2 × 10−5 s−1 in order to obtain the m-value at a nominal strain of 75%.

phases_and_microstructures.material_state: superplastically deformed (50% elongation at 673 K, low strain rate)

evidence.quote: In these specimens, pre-existing basal texture changed gradually toward random during high temperature deformation, though the basal texture was retained even after 75% elongation.

mechanisms.name: grain boundary sliding
mechanisms.material_state: superplastically deformed (50% elongation at 673 K, low strain rate)

evidence.quote: At the high temperatures, the material behaved in a superplastic manner at low strain rates, and dislocation creep dominated deformation at high strain rates.
It is probable that the m-value remained unchanged and thus the GBS is the dominant mechanism throughout deformation.
